evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心, 裘錫圭
evidence.field: discussion of 興 graph structure and ancient forms
evidence.text: The article argues that 興 depicts people jointly lifting a heavy object, but cautions that the object and its name cannot be confidently identified. It notes that an abbreviated 興-like form occurs in Wu Ding period oracle-bone inscriptions and discusses forms with an added 口; it treats the received 說文 analysis 从舁从同 as an old interpretive account, not settled proof of the original structure. It explicitly allows that the object’s name might have been 興, 同, or another word. The article discusses a later inscriptional reading of 興 as rising/recovering from illness, but does not establish a complete dated sequence of senses.
evidence.kind: scholarly article discussing primary inscriptional evidence
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：大豊（禮）簋銘新釋

evidence.text: The page labels its sequence oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and standard forms. Its text says the ancient forms comprise 舁 and 同 and resemble two people’s four hands lifting a mold; it says the standard form resembles small seal. This is the source’s graphic interpretation, not independent confirmation of the depicted object.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 興

It labels the image public domain and links the exact original SVG at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/34/%E8%88%88-seal.svg. The file is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

evidence.text: The supplied local Unihan rows report xìng for both 興 and 兴 (sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; field kMandarin). The inspected official U+8208 record is https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=8208 and dossier evidence reports kMandarin xìng plus simplified variant U+5174. The direct U+5174 page was not verified in this research pass. These are current readings, not evidence for ancient sound relations.

evidence.title: Unihan data for U+8208

evidence.text: The supplied local row gives 興 MC xing, OC *qʰ(r)əŋ, gloss “lift, rise” (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 興). This differs from the separately reported Zhengzhang form *qʰɯŋ; the notations are system-specific. Since no phonetic component is established in the inspected formation sources, this host reconstruction does not establish a component-to-host sound relation.

search_audit.outcome: Search returned a textbook-style lifting-tool interpretation and a specialist discussion. The specialist source cautions that the object's exact identity/name is uncertain.

gaps: The Fudan article reports an abbreviated 興-like oracle-bone form in Wu Ding period inscriptions, but this pass did not independently inspect an artifact image or establish a full graphic chronology.

The precise central object depicted in ancient forms and its original spoken name remain uncertain; source explanations include mold or lifting platform, while specialist discussion warns against assuming the object’s name was 同 or 興.

The dossier reports distinct early textual uses and received dictionary glosses, but this pass did not independently verify dated manuscript attestations or establish chronology among rising, recovery, mobilization, flourishing, and poetic 興 senses.

No phonetic component is independently supported by the sources inspected. The dossier’s 型 analysis remains unverified and conflicts with accounts treating 舁 and the center as semantic/graphic constituents. No phonetic borrowing claim is established.
A direct official Unihan record for U+5174 was not opened in this pass; the provided local row reports xìng. Local file paths identify the supplied row but are not external sources.

The direct Commons SVG URL was established through the exact inspected description page, but the web tool returned an internal error when opening the binary asset. It is a modern seal-style redraw, not a historical artifact image.
The inspected sources do not establish rights for a versioned bulk text extract; use concise page-specific paraphrase rather than a tracked corpus extract.
